facts.summary: Employers withhold an additional 0.9% employee Medicare tax on wages over $200,000 in a year (no employer match).
facts.evidence_quote: Employers are responsible for withholding the 0.9% Additional Medicare tax on an individual's wages paid in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year, without regard to filing status.
facts.source_title: Topic no. 751, Social Security and Medicare withholding rates
facts.source_publisher: Internal Revenue Service

facts.summary: FUTA tax is 6.0% on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages.
facts.evidence_quote: The FUTA tax rate is 6.0%. The tax applies to the first $7,000 you paid to each employee as wages during the year.
facts.source_title: Topic no. 759, Form 940, Employer's Annual Federal Unemployment (FUTA) Tax Return
facts.source_publisher: Internal Revenue Service

facts.summary: With the maximum 5.4% state credit, the FUTA rate is 0.6%.
facts.evidence_quote: If you're entitled to the maximum 5.4% credit, the FUTA tax rate after credit is 0.6%.
facts.source_title: Topic no. 759, Form 940, Employer's Annual Federal Unemployment (FUTA) Tax Return
facts.source_publisher: Internal Revenue Service

facts.summary: FUTA wage base is $7,000 per employee per year.

facts.value: immediately at the time of termination (including accrued vacation)
facts.summary: California: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately at the time of termination (including accrued vacation).
facts.evidence_quote: An employee who is discharged must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, immediately at the time of termination. Labor Code Sections 201 and 227.3
facts.source_title: Paydays, pay periods, and the final wages (California DIR, Labor Commissioner's Office)
facts.source_publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement
facts.notes: Industry exceptions exist (seasonal food processing, motion pictures, oil drilling, venue hiring halls) per the same page.

facts.value: at the time of quitting if 72 hours notice was given; otherwise within 72 hours of quitting
facts.summary: California: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due at the time of quitting if 72 hours notice was given; otherwise within 72 hours of quitting.
facts.evidence_quote: An employee without a written employment contract for a definite period of time who quits without giving 72 hours prior notice must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, within 72 hours of quitting. Labor Code Section 202
facts.source_title: Paydays, pay periods, and the final wages (California DIR, Labor Commissioner's Office)
facts.source_publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement
facts.notes: With at least 72 hours prior notice, wages are due at the time of quitting (Labor Code 202, same page).

facts.value: Yes: most employers must obtain coverage from the WY DWS Workers' Compensation Division; certain employers and employee groups are exempt and may buy private coverage.
facts.summary: Wyoming is a monopolistic state: most employers must get workers' comp from the state fund (DWS Workers' Compensation Division); exempt employers and groups may buy private coverage.
facts.evidence_quote: In Wyoming, most employers must obtain workers' compensation coverage through the Department of Workforce Service Workers' Compensation Division. This is because Wyoming is a monopolistic state, where the state fund is the primary provider of this insurance. However, certain employers and employee groups are exempt from this requirement. These exempt employers may purchase workers' compensation insurance from private insurers on the open market
facts.source_title: Workers' Compensation (Wyoming Department of Insurance)
facts.source_publisher: Wyoming Department of Insurance
